California is Yu-Gi-Oh! country, and today, Championship Dueling returns to the Golden State!

In 2018 an impressive 1411 Duelists gathered here to compete for their shot at Championship gold, in the first-ever Yu-Gi-Oh! Championship Series in Pasadena. It was a hotly competitive event, but in the end
soared over the field and claimed victory with Sky Strikers. One year later in 2019, even
Duelists came to Pasadena to test their mettle: 1607 competitors took their shot at the title, and Kobe Short came out on top with another win for Sky Strikers.

Today we’re back, and it’s been three years since the last Yu-Gi-Oh! Championship Series was held here in Pasadena. SoCal is undisputed as one of the world’s greatest Dueling communities, and in true California fashion this event has shattered records for previous YCS tournaments in the territory, with a current player count of 1716 attendees!
Two weeks ago we saw the Championship debut of the

booster set at YCS Minneapolis, ending in a stunning fourth YCS win for legendary Duelist Chris LeBlanc. It was like watching destiny in motion: LeBlanc captured his fourth title almost exactly ten years to the day after his first win at YCS Providence in 2012. In a weekend-long war between Spright and Tearlaments, LeBlanc united both strategies into one Deck; his build went all in on
. The result was a decisive victory in the Finals, where LeBlanc clipped the wings off Michael Tamez’s Floowandereeze to take home his trophy.
But time marches on! This weekend marks the first Championship appearance of
